title: Treasury's machine-learning check-fraud detection recovers $1 billion in FY2024
summary: Treasury reported over $4 billion in fraud and improper payments prevented or recovered in FY2024, including $1 billion recovered through machine-learning check-fraud detection.
account: On 17 October 2024 the U.S. Department of the Treasury announced that enhanced fraud-detection processes at the Bureau of the Fiscal Service's Office of Payment Integrity, including machine-learning AI, prevented and recovered over $4 billion in fraud and improper payments in Fiscal Year 2024 (October 2023 to September 2024), against a $652.7 million comparison figure for FY2023. The release breaks the total into $1 billion recovered through machine-learning identification of Treasury check fraud, $2.5 billion from identifying and prioritizing high-risk transactions, $500 million from expanded risk-based screening and $180 million from payment-processing efficiencies. Nextgov reported that the office uses machine learning to examine large amounts of data and flag potential fraudulent schemes, and NBC News reported that a Treasury official declined to give specific deployment examples for security reasons. No independent audit of the figures and no vendor or technique appears in the sources; the date used is the announcement date.

ratings.reason: The sources give only aggregate FY2024 totals for taxpayers' money recovered or prevented; no outcome is documented for an identifiable group.
Treasury reports aggregate prevention and recovery figures for the Office of Payment Integrity; no single deployment outcome is described.

ai_role.statement: Treasury's release attributes $1 billion of FY2024 recoveries to machine-learning AI that expedited identification of Treasury check fraud and $2.5 billion to prioritizing high-risk transactions; the technique is not described and no vendor is named, so developer and deployer appear to be the same public body (the Bureau of the Fiscal Service's Office of Payment Integrity) but this is not stated. The figures have not been independently verified in the sources.
